newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products pressured by US-sparked crude fal.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products pressured by US-sparked crude fal.

text.p: Mediterranean oil product markets came under pressure on Wednesday from the fall in crude sparked by bearish U.S. oil inventory data, traders said.

Sentiment on the gasoline market was softer with reports of a large U.S. stock build lending a bearish tone to markets on both sides of the Atlantic. Cif premium unleaded material was assessed some $1.00 to $2.00 weaker at $212/$213 a tonne.
The local market remained fairly tight and good demand was seen particularly for lower spec material into the eastern Med.
Naphtha strengthened, playing a late catch-up to crude's gains. The market for large cargoes was seen tight with a bid for pipeline spec material at $179 a tonne cif Med.
Gas oil prices were weaker with differentials to benchmark quotes under pressure as good avails saw most products well offered and buyers relaxed.
Traders said avails were beginning to grow as expected with refiners coming out of maintenance and with little opportunity to arbitrage product out of the region.

Premiums to benchmark quotes for 0.2 pct cargoes were slightly weaker with Russian cargoes talked around quotes high evens to +$1 cif Genoa. Premiums for well supplied EN590 remained soft at fob EN590 high quotes +$1-$2 a tonne.

Fuel oil was supported by bunker demand but little of the available Russian straight-run material was deemed appropriate by potential buyers. Nor did refiners show much interest in the healthy flow of Black Sea material.
High sulphur markets looked better supplied later in the month, but speculation persists on possible arbitrage cargoes being worked to the Far East, which could soak up material.
Although north-west Europe is supported by such talk many doubt the Med-Asia transit can be made profitably.
The one percent market was extremely quiet and prices tracked northern European swaps and cargo quotes.
